engine.name: Delhi Apartment Ownership Act 1986 + model bye-laws
recommended: Notice must be at least 2 and not more than 7 days before an annual or special meeting (model bye-law 16)
Quorum is a majority of owners in person, counted by votes (51%) per the Declaration (model bye-laws 10, 3(f))
Votes must be cast in person: no proxies (model bye-law 11)
If no quorum, adjourn at least 48 hours; at the adjourned meeting any two owners in person are enough (model bye-law 17)
An owner more than 60 days in arrears on the last day of the previous year cannot vote or stand for the Board (model bye-law 8)
Send a copy of every meeting notice to the Registrar / housing Commissioner (model bye-law 16)
gaps: Product cannot express 'owners in person count of persons vs votes' quorum split (the bye-laws say 'majority of owners' but define majority by votes)
Product cannot express a different notice rule for meetings of the Association vs 'copy to the Registrar'
Amendment of bye-laws needs 75 per cent of the total VALUE of units (bye-law 56): no special-majority threshold setting exists
Proxy ban is a model bye-law the Association can only vary with the Administrator's approval; not locked in the product because that approval route exists

recommended: AGM notice at least 15 days in writing with the audited accounts (Rules 2007 r.51); special meeting at least 7 days
Quorum is one-third of members, but never fewer than 10 members (r.48); this overrides the bye-laws

Committee elections must be by secret ballot run by a returning officer who is not a member or employee (s.35(2), Schedule II)
Committee fixes the election date at least 60 clear days before its term ends; nominations at least 7 clear days before the election (Schedule II)
Circulate minutes to all members within 15 days (housing societies, r.52(2))

The adjourned meeting must be held the same day, 15 minutes later: product's adjourned-minutes parameter is in hours
Poll by secret ballot only if one-third of members present demand it; otherwise show of hands: product's secret_ballot option is per event/point, not 'on demand'
Two-thirds-of-present special majority for bye-law amendment cannot be set as a fraction
Returning-officer rules (who may be appointed, Registrar appointment, security deposit, forfeiture) are not modelled

engine.name: Rajasthan Apartment Ownership Act 2015 + Model Bye-Laws 2020
recommended: General meeting quorum is two-thirds of Members, but electing, dissolving or removing the Management Committee needs three-quarters present (model bye-law 9(b)); the product has one quorum figure, so raise it to 75% for an election event.
If two-thirds do not come, the meeting may be adjourned for at least 24 hours; if there is again no quorum the meeting is dissolved (bye-law 14) - there is NO lower quorum at the adjourned meeting.
Proxy: in writing, handed to the Secretary/President at least 48 hours ahead; one proxy holder may act for only one member (bye-law 10).
Management Committee election: secret ballot paper, election officer appointed by the committee, two-year term (bye-law 39, 17).
A member more than 60 days in arrears on the day of the election can neither vote nor stand (bye-law 7(a)) - remove such flats from the voter list.
gaps: Different quorums for different business (2/3 general, 3/4 election/removal, 90% reserved matters) - the product holds one quorum per event.
Three majority classes (51% / two-thirds / 90% of ALL members) - the product's special-majority percentage is not a parameter and the 90%-of-total class cannot be expressed.
Arrears-over-60-days voting and candidacy ban is not an engine setting.
Proxy deadline of 48 hours before the meeting is not an engine setting.
Quorum is a whole fraction (two-thirds); loaded as 6666 basis points so that exactly that fraction of members satisfies it

recommended: Model bye-law 10: quorum is 30% of members present IN PERSON, so proxies do not count towards it (but may vote).
Notice is only two to seven days (bye-law 16), and a copy must also go to the Competent Authority or Registrar.
If quorum fails: adjourn for at least 48 hours; at the adjourned meeting 25% of owners or two owners (whichever is higher) form the quorum (bye-law 17).
Votes are weighted by the percentage in the Declaration (bye-law 9).
An owner more than 60 days in arrears at the end of the previous year cannot vote or stand for the Board (bye-law 8).

Majority wording is ambiguous (majority of those voting vs 51% of all votes), so the majority basis was left unset.
The 2/3-of-units approval for amending bye-laws (plus Competent Authority approval) cannot be expressed.
Arrears ban measured at the end of the previous year is not an engine setting.

recommended: No proxies (s.19): every member votes in person, one vote each (s.18).
Annual meeting within six months of the financial year end (s.24); 15 days' clear notice with the agenda (Rule 80).
Quorum figure of one-fourth of members or 500, whichever is less, is the rules' minimum bye-law content (Appendix B Part C); check your registered bye-laws.
If there is no quorum after one hour the meeting is reconvened after notice; at the reconvened meeting those present after one hour form the quorum (Appendix B Part A rule 6).
Committee election: secret ballot, one vote per voter, ties by lot, run by a Returning Officer appointed by the Registrar (Appendix C).
A member who attended fewer than two of the last five general meetings, or joined less than nine months ago, cannot vote in the general-meeting election (s.18 proviso).
Seats are reserved by law: one for scheduled castes and two for women (s.26(1)).
gaps: Elections are run by a Returning Officer appointed by the Registrar - the product's election officer is chosen by the Organizer.
Eligibility to vote depends on past attendance and minimum service use (s.18 proviso) - not an engine setting.
Quorum 'one-fourth or 500 whichever is less' is expressed with quorum.capFlats = 500; check the cap logic before use.
Reserved seats (1 SC, 2 women) are not a seat-by-seat feature.

Staggered Board terms (3/2/1 years) are not representable; only a single term value is.
Competent Authority notice and attendance (by-law 15A) is not a field.

electionRoles.source: https://www.thc.nic.in/Tripura%20State%20Lagislation%20Rules/Tripura%20Cooperative%20Societies%20Rules,%201976.pdf rule 61(1)-(9) (1978 substitution)

termYears.note: Committee term: such term, not exceeding three years, as the bye-laws prescribe (s.67 as in the PRS copy). Later amendments (for example aligning with the 97th Amendment) were not seen, so the three-year ceiling may have changed.
termYears.source: https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/acts_states/tripura/1974/1974TRIPURA8.pdf s.67

eligibility.value: Ineligible for the committee if in default to the society, interested in a contract with it, insolvent, legal practitioner against the society, jailed for moral turpitude, of unsound mind, a minor, a paid employee, or no longer a member. President, vice-president, chairman, secretary, treasurer: barred after two consecutive terms in that office
eligibility.source: https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/acts_states/tripura/1974/1974TRIPURA8.pdf ss.66-68

defaulterDisqualification.value: Default to the society in respect of any loan, advance or other dues bars election to the committee (clause (a) of s.66(1); the end of the clause is cut off in the scan)
defaulterDisqualification.note: 'Other dues' may include maintenance charges; not tested.
defaulterDisqualification.source: https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/acts_states/tripura/1974/1974TRIPURA8.pdf s.66(1)(a)

requisition.note: One-fifth of the members OR the smaller number the bye-laws specify.

reservedSeats.note: One seat for SC/ST and two for women on every elected committee of a society of individuals (all societies including credit-structure ones). Maximum 11 elected members for societies other than credit-structure societies.

notes: Rule 52: committee elects its President/Vice-President etc. by ballot; ballot papers kept three months.
Rule 53: annual accounts within 30 days of the close of the co-operative year (or extended period).

engine.name: Tripura co-operative society (Act 1974 / Rules 1976, amended)

proxy_voting.reason: Tripura Co-operative Societies Act 1974 s.27(1)(b): every member votes in person, no proxy

weightage.reason: Tripura Co-operative Societies Act 1974 s.27(1)(a): no member has more than one vote

recommended: Annual general meeting within three months of the accounts date, extendable by the Registrar (s.71(1)).
Special meeting: one-fifth of members (or fewer if your bye-laws say) can force one; committee must call it within one month (s.72).
Reserve one seat for SC/ST and two for women (Third Amendment 2016).
Committee elections are by secret voting (s.65(2)); candidates can withdraw up to seven days before the general meeting (Rule 61(8) as substituted 1978).
term.maxConsecutive 2 applies to office-bearer posts only (s.68).
gaps: General-meeting notice period and quorum are not in the text read - enter them from your bye-laws.
Term of the committee is 'up to 3 years per bye-laws' in the copy read: the product holds a single number, left blank.
Requisition is 'one-fifth or the smaller number in the bye-laws': only the one-fifth is held.
Tripura Apartment Ownership Act 1986 gives no numbers.
The two-consecutive-terms limit applies only to office-bearer posts, not to every committee seat; the product's term.maxConsecutive cannot say that, so it is left unset
